items.title: Open-Sourcing Rebalancer: A Generic, High-Performance Library for Solving Assignment Problems
items.content_snippet: We’re open-sourcing Rebalancer , the assignment-problem solver that has been used to solve resource allocation problems throughout Meta for over nine years. Rebalancer separates several related concerns: how to specify an assignment problem, how to store it efficiently in memory, how to solve it, and how to debug it. items.title: Figma Gave GPT-6 Astra a Moonshot. Here's what happened.
items.content_snippet: John gave GPT-6 Astra a moonshot: design the flight-control experience for a new personal aircraft. The gap between generating an interface and designing a system is massive, and AI models have always fallen short. Until now. Astra reasoned through the audience, jobs to be done, pilot-versus-passenger tradeoffs, and critical interface states. Then it connected that thinking to a real design system via the Figma MCP Server to create a polished, on-brand prototype of the concept.

items.title: “A Jaw Drop. Literally.” How Cooley Is Reimagining IPOs with OpenAI
items.content_snippet: “How do we save time and effort and energy for our clients?” For David Wang, Cooley’s Chief Innovation Officer, that question is central to IPO preparation, when information requests, drafting sessions, and reviews place heavy demands on senior executives. With GO Public, built on OpenAI technology, Cooley can get substantive work in front of clients sooner and spot issues earlier. People remain responsible for reviewing the output and standing behind the answers.

items.title: “It Blew Me Away” | Box’s First Look at GPT-6 Astra
items.content_snippet: A 20% incentive, counted twice, could throw off an entire cost analysis. Astra caught it. Yashodha Bhavnani (Box) gave GPT-6 Astra profit, cost, and tax-incentive files to work through. It recognized that one incentive was already included, and knew to leave it alone. Her first impression? “It blew me away.” Watch Yash in convo with Romain Huet, as they talk about what makes Astra different and what it means for customers working with their most complex content. Spoiler alert: Astra excels.

items.title: The Dark Arts of Skill Engineering — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek (Impeccable)
items.content_snippet: Paul Bakaus once turned the entire web orange. He wrote jQuery UI, shipped an orange default theme, assumed people would change it, and watched them not. So when he points out that the purple gradients everyone learned to mock came from a CSS framework's default sample page, and that AI generated design now has its own house shade of beige, he speaks as the cause rather than the critic. That history is what makes his central claim land. A ban does not produce originality, it relocates the model
